messages.text: This is terminal ileum: stem cells and Paneth cells sit at the crypt bases.

Terminal ileum (non-IBD control, diverticulitis). As you said, Paneth cells should sit at the crypt bases, but none were found: they are hidden inside "Stem cells". A sub-cluster of 536 stem cells (24%) has ITLN2 in 95% of its cells, KLK12 and SEC11C. The current Paneth markers (ITLN1, SPINK4) are goblet genes, so they could not pick these cells out. I propose new Paneth markers. Other problems: the NK cells are mostly TRDC+ KLRC2+ CD160+ γδ intraepithelial T cells (only 5 cells were called gd T); "Crypt-base fibroblasts" actually lie next to the muscle (median 826 µm from the epithelium), so I rename them by their markers; several markers are weak or unspecific (Effector/memory CD4, Goblet SPDEF, Enterocyte FABP2, Cycling TAs, Neutrophils, ILC IL7R, cDC2 ITGAX, Capillary EC, Blood vessel EC); Eosinophils and FDC are undetectable with this panel. Where the types lie mostly fits the priors (SI-03, SI-05, SI-08); the only finding is deep macrophages, monocytes and neutrophils (SI-09), probably real.
? M cells were not found (SPIB and CCL20 are not detected together). Are there Peyer's patches or a follicle-associated epithelium in this section? If not, M cells can be removed.
? Are crypt bases with Paneth cells visible across the whole section, or only in part of it? That helps judge how many Paneth cells to expect (the sub-cluster has 536 cells).

proposal.summary: Terminal ileum (non-IBD control, diverticulitis). As you said, Paneth cells should sit at the crypt bases, but none were found: they are hidden inside "Stem cells". A sub-cluster of 536 stem cells (24%) has ITLN2 in 95% of its cells, KLK12 and SEC11C. The current Paneth markers (ITLN1, SPINK4) are goblet genes, so they could not pick these cells out. I propose new Paneth markers. Other problems: the NK cells are mostly TRDC+ KLRC2+ CD160+ γδ intraepithelial T cells (only 5 cells were called gd T); "Crypt-base fibroblasts" actually lie next to the muscle (median 826 µm from the epithelium), so I rename them by their markers; several markers are weak or unspecific (Effector/memory CD4, Goblet SPDEF, Enterocyte FABP2, Cycling TAs, Neutrophils, ILC IL7R, cDC2 ITGAX, Capillary EC, Blood vessel EC); Eosinophils and FDC are undetectable with this panel. Where the types lie mostly fits the priors (SI-03, SI-05, SI-08); the only finding is deep macrophages, monocytes and neutrophils (SI-09), probably real.

edits.problem: Paneth cells hidden among Stem cells
edits.reason: You said Paneth cells sit at the crypt bases. They are inside Stem cells: requiring ITLN1 and SPINK4 (goblet genes, ITLN1 in 89% of goblet cells) meant no cell fit the Paneth type. ITLN2 is the Paneth-specific gene of the panel (HPA: Paneth-enriched; Nonnecke 2022); KLK12 and SEC11C mark the same sub-cluster.
edits.evidence: type_structure Stem cells /2: 536 cells, ITLN2 in 95% (45% of the other stem cells), KLK12 48% vs 6%, SEC11C 78% vs 33%; depth 0, sits apart (spatial clustering 1.53). ITLN2 in 3% of the non-stem epithelium (review_markers). In the Stem cells, ITLN2 is still a top gene (58% vs 3% of siblings).
edits.group: Paneth cells hidden among Stem cells

edits.markers: KLRF1+ NCAM1+ KLRD1+ NKG7+ CD3D- TRDC-
edits.problem: γδ intraepithelial T cells labelled NK cells
edits.reason: Half of the 'NK cells' are T cells: CD3E is in 48% and TRDC (TCR delta) in 56%. TRDC- keeps true NK cells.
edits.evidence: NK cells (341): TRDC 56% vs 3% of the other T/NK cells, CD3E 48%, KLRC2 68% vs 17%, CD160 40% vs 5%; 13.5% lie among epithelium (IELs, SI-08). gd T cells: only 5 cells.
edits.group: γδ intraepithelial T cells labelled NK cells

edits.problem: γδ intraepithelial T cells labelled NK cells
edits.reason: Ileal γδ IELs are TRDC+ with NK receptors (KLRC2, CD160). TRDV1 is rarely detected here, so I drop it and use the genes these cells show.
edits.evidence: In the current NK cells: TRDC 56%, KLRC2 68%, CD160 40%, each detected in at most 17% of the other T/NK cells.
edits.group: γδ intraepithelial T cells labelled NK cells

edits.problem: Fibroblast subtype named by a place where it does not lie
edits.reason: These cells do not lie at the crypt base: they lie near the muscle and in the submucosa. A type is better named by its markers.
edits.evidence: spatial_profile: median 826 µm from the epithelium, 61 µm from smooth muscle; 33% among smooth muscle cells; top genes GREM1 72%, SFRP2 63%, OGN 62%, C3 82%.
edits.group: Fibroblast subtype named by a place where it does not lie

edits.problem: Fibroblast subtype named by a place where it does not lie
edits.reason: SFRP2 is a sharp gene of this type.
edits.evidence: SFRP2 in 63% of them vs 1% of the telocytes.
edits.group: Fibroblast subtype named by a place where it does not lie

edits.reason: SOX6 and NRG1 are detected in few of these cells; EDNRB separates them from the other fibroblasts.
edits.evidence: SOX6 17%, NRG1 15%; EDNRB 43% vs 6%. 51% lie among epithelium: the subepithelial position telocytes are expected to have (SI-11).

edits.reason: KLRB1 and GZMK do not separate these cells from Tregs and naive CD4 T cells (the type is flagged weak: its markers are in 24% of its cells vs 23% of the other T/NK cells). CD69 marks tissue-resident memory.
edits.evidence: KLRB1 26% vs 19%, GZMK 8% vs 5%; CD69 48% vs 20%, CCL5 45% vs 15%.

edits.reason: SPDEF is detected in only 8% of goblet cells. ITLN1, REP15 and ERN2 (MUC2-pathway genes) mark them well.
edits.evidence: SPDEF 8%; ITLN1 89% vs 34%, REP15 62% vs 14%, ERN2 70% vs 23%.

edits.question: Should goblet cells that show enterocyte genes (APOB, MGAM) go to Enterocytes? They may also be goblet cells with transcripts spilled from neighbouring enterocytes on the villi.
edits.reason: One goblet sub-cluster expresses enterocyte genes.
edits.evidence: type_structure Goblet cells /3: 430 cells, APOB 83% vs 17%, MGAM 70% vs 14%, sits apart (2.77).

edits.reason: FABP2 is in most epithelial cells. SLC26A3 is specific.
edits.evidence: FABP2 90% vs 69% of siblings; SLC26A3 53% vs 8%.

edits.reason: PCLAF and UBE2C are detected in few cells.
edits.evidence: PCLAF 13%, UBE2C 20%; RRM2 53% vs 5%, TYMS 47% vs 5%.

edits.markers: RORC+ KIT+ IL1R1+ ALDOC+ CD3E- KLRF1-
edits.reason: IL7R is in most T cells too.
CXCR2 and CMTM2 are detected in few cells.
edits.evidence: CXCR2 19%, CMTM2 7%; MGAM 45% vs 1%, S100A12 27% vs 1%.

edits.reason: PLVAP is shared with venous EC.
PECAM1 and VWF are in lymphatic EC too.
edits.evidence: PECAM1 91% vs 79%, VWF|PLVAP 89% vs 71%; NOTCH4 50% vs 1%, PLVAP 63% vs 6%.

edits.reason: PECAM1 is detected in 35% of pericytes, spilled from the endothelial cells they wrap.
edits.evidence: PECAM1 35% vs 14%; pericytes neighbour arterial EC (log2 2.72).

edits.reason: CLC and CCR3 are hardly detected.
edits.evidence: Among 2,487 myeloid cells: CLC in 5 cells, CCR3 in 2.

edits.question: Remove FDCs? FDCSP is barely detected, and the B-cell area here is small.
edits.reason: No FDC cluster: FDCSP is in 168 cells, and CLU is broad (venous EC, ICC, glia).
edits.evidence: FDCSP in 168 of 56,852 cells (23 with 2+ transcripts).

questions: M cells were not found (SPIB and CCL20 are not detected together). Are there Peyer's patches or a follicle-associated epithelium in this section? If not, M cells can be removed.
Are crypt bases with Paneth cells visible across the whole section, or only in part of it? That helps judge how many Paneth cells to expect (the sub-cluster has 536 cells).

findings.where: median 715 µm from the epithelium, 158 µm from smooth muscle; monocytes median 1,400 µm; 11% among fibroblasts, 9% among smooth muscle
findings.rule: SI-09: Macrophages and most DCs fill the lamina propria of villi and crypts
findings.evidence: SI-09 itself says muscularis and submucosal macrophages are normal. Monocytes and neutrophils next to venous EC (log2 2.2–3.0) deep in the wall fit diverticulitis inflammation. Plasma cells and DCs do sit in the lamina propria (median 20–27 µm).
findings.key: macrophages, monocytes, neutrophils|si-09: macrophages and most dcs fill the lamina propria of villi and crypts|macrophages|fibroblasts
